beats.text: The deposit didn't come. No letter, no call. It's usually one of four things, and only one is about money.
One: a return wasn't filed. Yours, or your spouse's. No return, no benefit.
Two: your income went up. Every July the CRA recalculates from last year's return, so a raise shows up a year later.
Three: your marital status changed. Dana got married in March twenty twenty-six. She has to tell the CRA by the end of April.
Her new spouse's income gets added, and the benefit is adjusted starting the month after the change.
Four: a child turned eighteen, and that child's benefit stops. The twist: only one of the four is about how much you earn.
So check your messages in My Account before you call.
Next: is a second job worth it after tax and benefit cuts? Follow so you don't miss it.
